concerns.text: T008 (fetcher) is marked [P] but explicitly depends on T005 (memory_monitor) for clamping logic. T012 (roi_extractor) depends on T008. T013 (smoothing) depends on T012. These tasks form a strict linear chain (T005 -> T008 -> T012 -> T013) and CANNOT run in parallel. Marking them [P] violates the 'Producer before consumer' rule.

T007 (ReplicationResult entity) is marked [P] but depends on T006 (SimulationConfig entity) as stated in the description. Entities often share base types or config structures; if T007 imports T006, they cannot be parallelized. Even if independent, the description explicitly states 'Depends on T006', making the [P] tag incorrect.

T010 (Contract Test) and T011 (Integration Test) are marked [P] but depend on T006 and T012-T017 respectively. Tests cannot run before the code they test is implemented. The [P] tag implies they can run concurrently with implementation, which is logically impossible for TDD (Test-Driven Development) where tests fail until implementation exists.

T029 (Multi-Paradigm Runner) is marked [P] but depends on T022 (Power Curve Generator). T029 orchestrates the loop calling T022. An orchestrator cannot run in parallel with the logic it orchestrates; it must wait for T022 to be implemented and available.

T031b (Temporal Sensitivity Orchestrator) is marked [P] but depends on T031 (Parameter Injection). T031b calls T022 with specific parameters defined in T031. The dependency chain T031 -> T031b prevents parallel execution.

T038 depends on T038b, but T038b is listed in Phase 2a. The dependency arrow in T038 points to T038b, which is correct, but the [P] tag on T038 is misleading if T038b is a prerequisite for the final report generation. Ensure T038 is not marked [P] if it requires the output of T038b to be complete.
